chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Publisher songs, new arrangers, and more time for Ella
summary: Shapiro-Bernstein and Mills also supplied songs; McRae hired Jimmy Mundy and Van Alexander and gave Ella more broadcast time.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Bernstein -- all these companies were giving us top songs, you know.
Yeah, Shapiro-Bernstein. Shapiro and Bernstein. That's a big publishing company (Unaudible).
And a few other big companies, you know. They were giving us the top songs.
Yeah. We were getting a little --
So I got Jimmy Mundy. I hired this boy, Van Alexander. He called himself Van. He used to be something else then.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And we began to give Ella Fitzgerald most of the broadcast time. Like, she would just sing one song, we would have her doing three -- sometimes four.
And this moved her up. And then people started taking notice of that, see. Especially the bands downtown.
They say, 'Hey, how yall get those songs?' You know, we were getting them before anybody, you know.
